ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #13
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

2. When practising Speaking Fluency: pronunciation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.

3. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.

   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.

4. When practising Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.

   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.

5. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. No full stops
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

6. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

7. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.

8. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. went
   C. goed
   D. goes

9. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

10. When practising Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

11. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the library
   C. Where is the Library
   D. Where is the library?

12. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.

13. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.

14. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. quickly
   C. happiness
   D. run

15. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only an action
   C. Only a describing word
   D. Only a joining word
